See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Required next GPA = [Target × (Current credits + Next credits) − Current GPA × Current credits] ÷ Next credits

A worked example

A current 3.20 GPA across 45 credits, a 3.30 cumulative target and a 15-credit next term require (3.30 × 60 − 3.20 × 45) ÷ 15 = 3.60 next term.

Before you use the result

Both records must use the same grade-point scale and credit system. Enter only GPA-bearing credits. The selected maximum determines whether the required next GPA is possible. Rounded current GPAs introduce estimation error, and retake replacement is not applied.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

What if the required GPA is above my scale?

The target is not reachable in that number of credits under the selected maximum. A longer timeline or lower target may be needed.

Can I use this across different GPA scales?

No. Current, future and target GPA must all use the same scale.
